chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ubays ibn Hisham, from Thabit, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the child of al-mu'lanah (cursing) when they cursed each other and separated, and her husband said afterwards, 'The child is my child,' while he was lying about himself. He (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the woman, she does not return to him, but I return the child to him, and I do not leave him as his son; he has no inheritance. If his father does not claim him, then his maternal uncles inherit him, and they do not inherit from him. If anyone claims him as the son of adultery, he is whipped with the limit punishment.'

key_terms.الْحَدَّ: The limit punishment (specifically flogging in this context).
key_terms.الْمُلَاعَنَة: Al-mu'lanah: The procedure of mutual cursing between husband and wife to establish or deny paternity.

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance status of a child from al-mu'lanah if the father denies paternity?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the specific inheritance dynamics of a child from *al-mu'adah* (cursing), where the child is returned to the father but excluded from his direct lineage for inheritance purposes, reverting to the maternal uncles if unclaimed. It highlights the Shia juristic distinction between paternity (*nasab*) and inheritance (*mirath*), ensuring the child's status is preserved while protecting the husband's rights. The ruling also enforces the penalty of *hadd* for false claims of illegitimacy, reinforcing the legal finality of the cursing procedure.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Ubays Bin Hisham, from Sabit, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a child of the mother cursed by her husband, when she was cursed and separated, and her husband said after that, ‘The child is my child, and I lied myself’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for the woman, so she would not return to him, but the child is returned to him and would not be called as his son. There is no inheritance for him if its father does not claim him. Thus, its maternal uncle would inherit him and he would not inherit them. So if anyone were to call him as being a son of adultery, he would be whipped the Limit’.
en.sarwar: 10. Abu Ali a l-Ash ‘ariy has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Kufiy from ‘Ubays ibn Hisham from Thabit from abu Basir who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who forms Mula ‘anah against his wife, then they separate from each other. The husband thereafter says that the child is his child and he calls himself a liar. He (the Imam) said, ‘The woman cannot return to him but the child must be joined with him; he cannot skip the child. There is no inheritance for him and if his father does not claim him, then his maternal uncles inherit him but he does not inherit them (maternal uncles). If anyone calls him a son of fornication, such a person must be subjected to whipping as a penalty.’” [Note: The next several passages of the Arabic text are words of al-Fadl and are not translated.]
